inputs.value:
DIRECT CONTINUATION OF THE PREVIOUS SCENE.

CHARACTER REFERENCES:

<Picture 1> = S1, the Asian woman.
<Picture 2> = S2, the young white man.
<Picture 3> = S3, the jealous ex-girlfriend.

Preserve exact facial identity, facial structure, hairstyle, apparent age, skin tone, body proportions, clothing, and continuity from every previous scene.

This begins immediately after S2 says, "I was afraid you'd leave."

S1 is deeply hurt and angry. She decides she cannot continue the argument and leaves the apartment.

S2 desperately tries to explain himself and follows her toward the door, but he does not physically restrain her.

Same damaged living room after the earthquake. Fallen television, tipped lamp, scattered popcorn, spilled drinks, dim nighttime lighting.

Only close-up, tight close-up, medium close-up, and half-body shots. No wide shots. No full-body shots.

Maximum 60 spoken English words. Keep dialogue sparse and allow silence, movement, facial reactions, and emotion to carry the scene.

[Shot 1 — 00:00–00:05]

Tight close-up of S1.

She absorbs S2's words in silence.

Her eyes are hurt and disappointed.

She takes a slow breath and looks away.

S2 steps closer into the edge of frame.

S2 says urgently:

<d>[English] S1, please. Let me explain.</d>

S1 shakes her head.

She quietly answers:

<d>[English] I need to go.</d>

She turns away from him.

S2 looks devastated.

[Shot 2 — 00:05–00:10]

Medium close-up / half-body tracking shot.

S1 quickly gathers her belongings from the sofa and coffee table.

She picks up her phone and bag.

S2 follows a few steps behind her.

S2 says:

<d>[English] It wasn't what you think.</d>

S1 stops briefly.

She turns toward him.

Her expression is deeply frustrated.

S1 says:

<d>[English] Then why didn't you tell me?</d>

S2 struggles to answer.

He takes a breath.

S2 says:

<d>[English] I should have.</d>

S1 looks away.

[Shot 3 — 00:10–00:15]

Tight half-body shot near the apartment doorway.

S1 puts on her jacket.

Her movements are quick and determined.

S2 stands several feet away, visibly anxious.

S2 says:

<d>[English] I was going to tell you.</d>

S1 looks at him.

S1 replies:

<d>[English] When?</d>

Silence.

S2 has no immediate answer.

S1 opens the apartment door.

She hesitates for the smallest moment, looking back at him.

Then she steps through.

S2 remains inside.

[Shot 4 — 00:15–00:20]

Tight cinematic tracking shot following S1 from close behind and then shifting to her face as she moves through the building hallway toward the exit.

S2 follows to the doorway, still trying to explain himself.

S2 calls after her:

<d>[English] Please, wait!</d>

S1 keeps walking.

The building is dim and quiet after the earthquake. Emergency lights and distant city light enter through the windows.

S1 reaches the building entrance.

She pauses at the door.

For a brief moment, she looks back toward S2 in the distance.

Their eyes meet.

S1 looks heartbroken.

Then she opens the door and leaves.

S2 stops at the doorway, unable to follow immediately.

He watches the door close.

End at 20.00 seconds.

EMOTIONAL PERFORMANCE:

S1 is not simply angry anymore. She feels betrayed and emotionally overwhelmed.

Her decision to leave should feel like a painful choice rather than a dramatic tantrum.

She avoids looking at S2 because looking at him makes leaving harder.

S2 becomes increasingly desperate as he realizes she is actually leaving.

He wants to explain himself but cannot find the right words.

His frustration should turn into fear of losing her.

Neither character screams.

No physical aggression.

No grabbing.

No blocking the doorway.

The emotional intensity comes from restraint.

FACIAL PERFORMANCE:

S1:

Hurt eyes.

Tense jaw.

Controlled breathing.

Brief moments of vulnerability.

Forced composure while putting on her jacket.

A final lingering look toward S2 before leaving.

S2:

Anxious expression.

Regret.

Uncertainty.

Attempts to maintain eye contact.

Visible realization that his explanation may have come too late.

CAMERA:

Use intimate handheld cinematic camera language.

Shot 1: very tight emotional close-up.

Shot 2: restrained half-body tracking as S1 gathers her things.

Shot 3: intimate doorway composition.

Shot 4: close tracking movement following S1 through the hallway toward the building entrance.

Keep the camera close to S1.

No wide establishing shots.

No full-body shots.

No distant views.

The camera should gradually feel farther emotionally even while remaining physically close: S1 moves away from S2 while he remains behind.

VISUAL STYLE:

Photorealistic live action.

Premium Hollywood relationship drama.

Natural skin texture.

Highly consistent facial identity.

Realistic eye movement.

Subtle micro-expressions.

Natural body mechanics.

Natural nighttime lighting.

Soft depth of field.

Realistic apartment and building environment.

Subtle cinematic film grain.

No soap-opera exaggeration.

No artificial crying.

overall_soundscape:

Quiet damaged apartment ambience.

Soft footsteps.

Clothing and jacket movement.

Bag and phone sounds.

Distant sirens following the earthquake.

Door hinges.

Hallway room tone.

S2's voice echoing slightly through the doorway.

The apartment becomes quieter as S1 moves farther away.

The building entrance door closes softly at the end.

non_diegetic_music:

Very restrained emotional piano begins after S1 says, "I need to go."

Add soft sustained strings as she gathers her belongings.

Music becomes slightly more emotional while she puts on her jacket.

As she walks through the hallway, reduce the score and allow footsteps and silence to dominate.

When S1 looks back at S2 for the final time, introduce one quiet piano chord.

End unresolved as the door closes.
